title: Your IPO Just Got a 'Big Investor' Stamp of Approval: Understanding Anchor Investors
description: Anchor investors are big institutional players like mutual funds or insurance companies who invest in an IPO a day before it opens to the public. They commit .

faq.q: Who can be an anchor investor?
faq.a: Only Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) as defined by SEBI are eligible to be anchor investors. This includes entities like mutual funds, insurance companies, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), and large banks.

faq.q: What is the minimum amount an anchor investor must invest?
faq.a: For a mainboard IPO, an anchor investor must invest a minimum of ₹10 crore. For SME IPOs, the minimum is ₹2 crore.

faq.q: When do anchor investors get their shares?
faq.a: Anchor investors are allotted shares one business day before the IPO opens for public subscription.

faq.q: What is the lock-in period for anchor investors?
faq.a: Currently, 50% of the shares allotted to anchor investors are locked in for 30 days from the allotment date, and the remaining 50% are locked in for 90 days.

faq.q: How does anchor investor participation help in price discovery?
faq.a: Their large, early bids within the price band provide an initial demand signal, helping the company and merchant bankers gauge investor interest and arrive at a fair final issue price for the IPO.
